en.title: iu in iubit (beloved)
en.summary: The diphthong iu is found in the Romanian word iubit.

sections.title: The sound of iu
paragraphs: The letters iu are called the sound /ju/. They make the sound /ju/ in (iubit) /juˈbit/, which means beloved. These two letters can make two different sound patterns.

sections.title: How to say iu
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift your tongue high and forward, then round your lips tightly. Your voice flows smoothly from a quick glide into the vowel. For the second sound, make two separate beats. Hold your tongue high and flat for the first beat. Then push your lips forward into a circle for the second beat. Place a hand on your throat to feel continuous vibration.

sections.title: Spelling rules for iu
paragraphs: When the two letters sit in one single syllable, they make the sound /ju/, as in (iute) /ˈju.te/. When each letter sits in its own syllable, you hear two clear vowels as the sound /i.u/, as in (știu) /ʃti.u/. This split also happens across syllables in (triumf) /triˈumf/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with iu
paragraphs: Do not swallow the first vowel when the pair splits into two beats. In words with two syllables, do not rush through the letters like the quick glide in you. Say each vowel fully, giving each its own clear pulse of voice.
